case_title: Dr. Vinod Bhandari v. State of M.P.
accused_occupation: Managing Director of a medical institute (Shri Aurbindo Institute of Medical Sciences, Indore)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.420, s.467, s.468, s.471, s.120B; MP Manyata Prapt Pariksha Adhiniyam 1937 s.3(d), s.1, s.2/4; IT Act s.65, s.66 (as listed in FIR; not confirmed as framed charges)
evidence_type: Documentary (excel data, seized documents, candidate lists, seizure memo of cash); statement under s.164 Cr.P.C.; co-accused memoranda
confession: Statement under s.164 Cr.P.C. by a candidate's parent is relied on by the State as incriminating; its weight was not decided by the Supreme Court
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged high-magnitude admission of large number of undeserving candidates by corrupt means; alleged depravity and generation of black money; alleged role as kingpin; alleged potential to influence witnesses
trial_court_outcome: Second bail application dismissed (no trial verdict; trial pending)
high_court_outcome: Division Bench dismissed bail application (order dated 11.08.2014, M.Cr.C. No. 10371 of 2014)
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleges a conspiracy to secure admission to undergraduate medical courses for candidates who had not earned places on merit. The scheme allegedly involved copying during a state professional entrance test, with some high-scoring persons seated among candidates so they could supply correct answers. Blank answer sheets were allegedly later filled in with correct answers by officials, and a model answer key was reportedly copied and passed to candidates one night before the examination. Each candidate reportedly paid several lakh rupees to middlemen, who shared the money with officials. The accused is alleged to have received money from candidates through a general manager of an institution connected with the accused, who handled admissions. During investigation, the general manager made a disclosure that led to the recovery of money and documents, including a seizure of cash. Seized material included a list of candidates sponsored from the accused's institution, electronic data from an examination board office, documents and activity charts from that board, and memoranda of other accused persons. A statement recorded under the criminal procedure code by a parent of a candidate said the accused had asked him to meet the general manager and pay a sum for admission, which he could not pay. The investigation involved a large number of accused persons, a substantial number of whom had been arrested, with further charge sheets pending.
offence_severity: Maximum: life imprisonment (as stated in the judgment); minimum not stated
physical_harm: None (no injury or death alleged); concern noted about risk to patients' health from unqualified doctors
number_of_offences: 10 charged (sections named in FIR; framed charges not stated); 0 finally upheld (bail matter, no conviction)
financial_property_loss: Alleged receipt of few crores of rupees by the accused; cash of Rs. 60 lakh seized from co-accused's general manager (per High Court recital)
premeditation_planning: Alleged pre-planned conspiracy; the Supreme Court did not decide this
motive: alleged: monetary gain from candidates paying for admission
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence was tested; the Supreme Court accepted at prima facie stage that the allegations are supported by material on record
post_offence_conduct: Noted by the High Court: went abroad after FIR registration and returned only after anticipatory bail (not decided by the Supreme Court)
custody_duration: About one year (as stated by the Supreme Court)
bail_history: Anticipatory bail granted 16.01.2014 in other FIR; first bail dismissed 05.02.2014; second bail dismissed 09.05.2014 by trial court; High Court dismissed 11.08.2014; Supreme Court disposed of appeal with liberty to apply afresh after one year if trial not completed for reasons not attributable to the appellant
trial_duration: offence: not given; FIR registered 30 October 2013; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 11.08.2014; Supreme Court: 04.02.2015
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: Siddharth Luthra, H. P. Raval, Kunal Verma, Keki Vajpei, Prasanna Mohan, Anando Mukherjee; State: Mishra Saurabh, Vanshaja Shukla, Ankit Kr. Lal
investigation_status: FIR registered 30.10.2013; 516 accused in all, 329 arrested, 187 to be arrested; charge sheets and supplementary charge sheets filed; final charge sheet directed by 15 March 2015 against remaining accused
appeal_history: Trial court: bail dismissed (09.05.2014). High Court: bail dismissed (11.08.2014). Supreme Court: appeal disposed of with directions and liberty to apply afresh if trial not completed in one year
prosecution_argument: Courts below considered nature of allegations, material, misuse of bail and societal impact; prima facie complicity; offence punishable with life; appellant was kingpin; potential to influence witnesses; investigation pending; earlier went abroad to avoid arrest
defence_argument: Prolonged custody of about one year; no prospect of early trial given 516 accused and many witnesses and documents; delay entitles appellant to bail
legal_principle_applied: Bail is refused where allegations are supported by material and bail could adversely influence trial; seriousness is not the only factor; delay is a relevant factor, and an accused cannot be kept in custody indefinitely if trial is unlikely to conclude within reasonable time
precedent_relied_upon: Kalyan Chandra Sarkar v. Rajesh Ranjan (2005) 2 SCC 42; State of U.P. v. Amarmani Tripathi (2005) 8 SCC 21; State of Kerala v. Raneef (2011) 1 SCC 784; Sanjay Chandra v. CBI (2012) 1 SCC 40
judicial_mitigating_factors: Prolonged custody of about one year and no prospect of immediate trial, which the Court treated as a matter of serious concern
judicial_aggravating_factors: High magnitude of offence; serious adverse impact on society; depravity of character and black money; potential to undermine trust in the medical profession; potential to influence trial if bail granted
other_sentence_order: Directions: trial to proceed day to day; High Court to review progress once every three months; trial to be completed within one year, failing which appellant may apply afresh for bail; observations not an opinion on merits
